introduction: Today we begin Advent and a new liturgical year, the year of Saint Luke's Gospel. Jeremiah promises a righteous Branch from David. Jesus speaks of signs in the heavens and tells us to stand up and raise our heads, because our redemption is near; he warns us not to let our hearts be weighed down. Paul prays that our love may increase. Let us begin this season watchful and full of hope.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord is coming, and our redemption is near. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church as she begins a new liturgical year: that she may wait for the Lord with joyful hope. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who are anxious about the future of the world: that they may lift up their heads in hope. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those whose hearts are weighed down by worries, addictions or excess: that they may find freedom and peace. Let us pray to the Lord.
For our families and communities: that our love for one another may increase and overflow. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may use this Advent to prepare our hearts for Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, at the beginning of this Advent, increase our love and keep us watchful in prayer, so that we may stand with confidence before your Son when he comes. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Lift up your heads
reflection.body:
A new liturgical year begins today. Over the coming year, most Sunday Gospels will come from Saint Luke, the evangelist of mercy, of the poor, and of prayer.

Advent begins not with Bethlehem but with the end of time. Jesus speaks of "signs in the sun, moon, and stars," of nations in anguish, and of people "fainting for fear." Yet his message is not fear but hope: "But when these things begin to happen, look up and lift up your heads, because your redemption is near." When everything seems to be shaking, Christians do not hide; they raise their heads to see their Lord coming.

Jesus also gives a very practical warning: "So be careful, or your hearts will be loaded down with carousing, drunkenness, and cares of this life." A heart can become heavy with too much pleasure or too much worry. Both make us forget what matters. So he says, "Therefore be watchful all the time, praying."

Jeremiah gives the promise behind our hope: "In those days and at that time, I will cause a Branch of righteousness to grow up to David." God keeps his word. The child born in Bethlehem is that Branch, and he will come again.

Paul tells us how to wait: not by doing nothing, but by loving more. "May the Lord make you to increase and abound in love toward one another and toward all men."

Advent is a gift: four weeks to lighten our hearts and prepare a place for Christ. This week, choose something that weighs your heart down and set it aside: an excess, a worry, a screen. Use the time to pray. And light the first candle of an Advent wreath at home, as a sign that you are watching for the Lord.
